description: Gate result: run_all_arms.sh — both arms of the paper's headline M4 comparison (Goodfellow et al. 2015, tex:492-494). Configuration: maxout 240x2, pieces 5, eps=0.25, alpha=0.5, 5000 SGD steps. NOTE: dropout is OFF (include 1.0/1.0) in this gate so the eps=0 degeneracy holds bit-for-bit (tests/test_degeneracy.py); the paper's M4 net was 'also regularized with dropout' (tex:492), so this gate is the degeneracy-valid form of the M4 comparison, NOT a dropout-on match to the paper's exact 0.94%->0.84% magnitudes (those need dropout ON + early stopping to convergence, in experiments/m4_adversarial.py). Each arm prints exactly one line `FINAL <arm>=<clean test accuracy>`.

paper_target.direction: adversarial training should reduce clean test error vs baseline (i.e. raise clean test accuracy)

value_definition: clean test accuracy = mean(argmax logits == y) over the 10k MNIST test set

config.threads: OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 MKL_NUM_THREADS=4 (PyTorch default pool over-spawns on multi-core; ~7x slowdown observed at 1500 steps)

result.note: adversarial arm clean accuracy (0.9829) > baseline clean accuracy (0.9788), i.e. adversarial training REDUCED clean test error (2.12% -> 1.71%), reproducing the DIRECTION of the paper's M4 headline claim (0.94% -> 0.84%, tex:492-494). This gate runs with dropout OFF (degeneracy validity), so it is NOT a magnitude match to the paper's dropout-on 0.94%->0.84%; the higher-fidelity dropout-on arm lives in experiments/m4_adversarial.py with committed results/m4_adversarial.json (baseline 1.98% -> adversarial 1.64%).

degeneracy.contract: --lambda 0 (arm 'adversarial' at its no-op) prints the SAME accuracy VALUE as --baseline (arm 'baseline'); names differ by construction

note_on_reproducibility: run_all_arms.sh is fully deterministic (torch.manual_seed before model construction; per-module dropout generator seeded from cfg.seed; batch shuffle via seeded torch.Generator). Same seed reproduces bit-identical FINAL lines. Runtime ~1-2 min under normal CPU load (measured 1m55s); under heavy multi-core contention the adversarial arm can be starved, but the numbers are reproducible and the gate script itself is load-independent.
